page.text:
When we restrict our attention to the collection of all subsets of a
fixed ambient set $U$—the power set $\mathcal{P}(U)$—the subset relation
imposes a rich structural architecture. Inclusion is reflexive,
antisymmetric, and transitive, endowing $\mathcal{P}(U)$ with the
structure of a partially ordered set (poset). In this order, the empty
set $\emptyset$ serves as the unique global minimum (since $\emptyset
\subseteq A$ for every $A$), and the ambient set $U$ serves as the unique
global maximum (since $A \subseteq U$ for every $A$).
